transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-15
Time: 14:00 - 14:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Saffron SRE), Maya Chen (Saffron ML), Ravi Patel (Saffron Product), Anika Gomez (Saffron QA)

Summary: Quick review of KV/prefix hit improvements, discussion of prompt reuse patterns that are reducing cold starts, retune of eviction TTLs and prefetch aggressiveness. Agreed to run a 2-hr benchmark and share configs.

Topics: KV hit rate delta, prefetch thresholds, session affinity, eviction policy, latency tail, next steps for pilot scaling, security/ops notes.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Morgan: hey everyone thanks for joining, can we do quick roll call?
[00:06] Tom: tom here, hey.
[00:07] Maya: maya on the call.
[00:08] Ravi: ravi here.
[00:09] Anika: anika.
[00:10] Priya: priya from redwood, hi all.
[00:12] Morgan: perfect ok, quick agenda — numbers review then tuning items and action items. Priya you want to kick off with hit rate?
[00:20] Priya: yeah, sure. so we ran the prefetch experiment last thursday and friday, the combined KV hit rate for top-20 prefixes is up to about 46% from baseline 18%. overall KV hit across traffic increased from ~22% to ~35% during active window, so decent lift. latency improved at p50 by ~9ms and p95 improved about 35ms, p99 improved but less consistent.
[00:43] Tom: can you repeat the p95 number? i caught 35ms.
[00:46] Priya: yep p95 ~35ms lower than baseline when prefetch was on. p99 dropped by 18ms on average but spiky during cold restarts.
[00:54] Maya: that is promising. are these numbers with the session affinity setting on or off?
[00:58] Priya: good q. these are with session affinity on for 60s; without affinity the hit rate dropped to ~29% but p50 similar. affinity helps keep local KV warm for short dialogs.
[01:10] Ravi: that session affinity has tradeoffs right? like it pins capacity or causes imbalance?
[01:14] Priya: correct — we saw slight imbalance across pods when affinity window was long (300s). at 60s it's negligible. if you need longer user conversations we'll need to consider sticky routing or connection pooling.
[01:25] Tom: interesting. our main worry is cost — more warmup means more GPU time?
[01:29] Morgan: yes, that's the cost/latency tradeoff. prefetch aggressiveness increases transient compute but reduces repeated decoding cost. our optimization suggestion is to prefetch only for sessions with high reuse probability — i.e., user flows where prompt templates match frequently.
[01:42] Anika: quick dumb q: when you say prefetch, is that loading KV per session or per model instance?
[01:46] Priya: it's per model instance but keyed by prefix hash. we prefetch the KV for the prefix on the worker that will serve the session.
[01:52] Anika: ok thanks.
[01:54] [02:05] Priya: on eviction TTLs — we prototyped a two-tier TTL: 90s for high frequency prefixes, 20s for low frequency ones based on moving window frequency. that reduced cold evictions by ~40% for top cohorts.
[02:20] Maya: how are you classifying high vs low freq? sliding window?
[02:22] Priya: sliding 30-minute window with decay; simple threshold on count. we can share the rule set.
[02:28] Ravi: will that be stable under bursty traffic like marketing campaigns?
[02:31] Priya: bursts cause temporary churn; we recommend adaptive thresholds that scale with qps. for campaigns you can pin prefixes or bump TTLs via routing rule.
[02:40] Tom: we noticed a weird behavior last night where hit rate dropped for a subset of prefixes after a deploy. could that be TTL related?
[02:46] Priya: possibly — deploys can cause node rotations and warm caches get invalidated. we have a grace rewarm mechanism but if TTLs are short you'll see drops. we can set a small pre-warm window during deploys to avoid that.
[02:58] Morgan: note — we will propose a deploy-safe config to avoid regressions.
[03:01] [03:18] Maya: about prompt reuse — we enumerated 230 unique templates, top 40 account for ~72% of production tokens. if we canonicalize those we should get better reuse.
[03:30] Priya: exactly, canonicalization + prefix hashing improves match. watch out for user-specific slots like {user_name} — those reduce reuse unless normalized.
[03:38] Ravi: are you suggesting we normalize placeholders at edge? that's on our side but we can do it. any gotchas?
[03:43] Priya: main gotcha is semantics: normalizing too aggressively might merge prompts that should be distinct. recommend a small whitelist of placeholders for normalization.
[03:51] Anika: we can do that for the top 40 templates, that's low lift.
[03:55] [04:12] Tom: security ops question — does prefetch touch any PII? our prompts sometimes contain email fragments in examples.
[04:18] Priya: prefetch is agnostic to content; Redwood doesn't retain user content beyond configured retention. for PII-sensitive flows enable redaction at the client side or use masked placeholders. we also support KMS integration for keying telemetry IDs in logs.
[04:32] Morgan: and we'll send SOC2 summary and our retention appendix after the call.
[04:36] [04:45] Maya: can we see a quick demo of the console numbers?
[04:48] Priya: sure, sharing screen — console link in chat: https://redwood.example/console/saffron/prefetch-2026-10-15 (placeholder)
[04:56] [05:10] Priya: here you can see hit rates by prefix cohort, p50/p95/p99 trends, and a little distribution of slot types. you can also toggle prefetch on per-prefix to see simulated impact.
[05:25] Ravi: the simulated impact looks optimistic vs our observed numbers, any reason?
[05:29] Priya: sim assumes steady-state reuse and no node drain. real-world has deploys and coldstarts; we add conservative fudge for planning.
[05:36] Tom: curious about the memory footprint of keeping KV for top-40 prefixes — do you have estimates?
[05:41] Priya: ballpark: top-40 would be ~3.2GB for this model family with 2k sequence avg; with quantized weights and sparse storage it's manageable on [dedicated] worker. we'll include memory numbers in the config doc.
[05:54] Anika: ok. QA will try to reproduce the p99 spikes. any guidance on test harness?
[05:59] Priya: use the workload-replay tool we shared earlier; run 30-minute window with injected deploys to see resilience. we'll attach the replay script.
[06:10] [06:28] Ravi: quick procurement note — if we move to dedicated we need a 30-day trial and clear metrics for SLA. is that supported?
[06:34] Morgan: yes we can do a 30-day reserved eval on dedicated with SLOs around latency and availability, and a side-by-side compare to hosted. i'll scope pricing as next step.
[06:44] Maya: for the benchmark run week of 10/27, what should we measure exactly?
[06:49] Priya: recommend p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, KV hit rate by cohort, compute cost per 10k tokens, and cold-start behavior under deploy. also capture quality regression via eval prompts.
[07:02] Tom: capture network egress patterns as well — we saw cross-region tails affecting p99 once.
[07:07] Priya: good call, include region breakdown.
[07:10] [07:24] Anika: small note — our QA found an intermittent serialization error when prefetch keys contain emojis, odd but reproducible.
[07:32] Priya: we saw that in earlier SDK versions; fixed in 0.9.3. are you on 0.9.1?
[07:36] Anika: yes 0.9.1, we'll upgrade and rerun.
[07:39] Morgan: we'll put the fixed SDK link in the notes.
[07:44] [08:00] Maya: about eviction policy, could you recommend an initial conservative config?
[08:04] Priya: suggestion: tier TTL = {high: 120s, mid: 45s, low: 15s}, prefetch threshold = 0.6 reuse probability, session affinity 60s, adaptive bump for sustained qps > baseline by 30%. we'll send as YAML in the shared doc.
[08:24] Ravi: that sounds reasonable. for the adaptive bump do you have a hysteresis to prevent flip-flopping?
[08:29] Priya: yes 5-minute hold window with 15% cooldown.
[08:33] Tom: any concerns about KMS or encryption for logs? procurement will ask.
[08:36] Morgan: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for log encryption in Private and Dedicated; hosted has managed keys but can be audited. we'll attach KMS note and compliance doc.
[08:46] [09:00] Priya: one more note — we recommend running a small canary of prefetch at 10% traffic first to validate assumptions, then ramp 30% -> 60% -> 100% if stable.
[09:12] Maya: ok we'll do 10% canary.
[09:15] Morgan: perfect. recap — priya sends config, tom uploads histograms, morgan sends pricing, schedule benchmark. any other items?
[09:25] Anika: QA will test serialization after SDK upgrade and report.
[09:28] Tom: procurement will follow up on contract language for the trial.
[09:31] Morgan: great, thanks everyone. meeting end.

References shared: console link (placeholder), shared drive folder: https://drive.google.com/saffron-poc (placeholder), config draft: https://redwood.example/docs/saffron-prefetch-config.yaml (placeholder).
